text:
maria.chen: quick RFC follow-up — i want to propose a 'warmup credit' abstraction for model warmup + decrypt/prefetch work in Private deployments. TL;DR: bounded background work so individual requests can't trigger huge NFS/HSM storms.

devin.k: can you sketch how it differs from existing prefetch/batch budget?

maria.chen: yes — today we have global prefetch threads + eviction heuristics. warmup-credit is per-model (and per-variant) budget that counts actual IO+decrypt CPU used by background warmups. credits refill slowly and are consumed by both background and on-request warmups. once exhausted, warmup work is sampled or queued behind router backpressure.

calvin: sounds useful for multi-tenant Dedicated too. how do we account for streaming safetensors + partial shards?

maria.chen: for streaming/safetensors we split work into small integrity windows (e.g., 64–256KB). each window consumption charges credits. benefit: streaming steady-state cost is predictable and we avoid one-off huge read+decrypt. also lets us favor prefix windows for decoder hot paths.

rachael: what about encrypted shards (KMS/HSM)? HSM latency spikes are scary.

maria.chen: exactly — HSM calls have a larger weight multiplier. sample config: 
```
warmup_policy:
  credits_per_minute: 50000  # bytes-equivalent units
  window_size_bytes: 65536
  hsm_multiplier: 8
  priority_buckets:
    - canary: 1
    - realtime: 2
    - bulk: 0.2
```

devin.k: nice. Pricing aside, how does this interact with index-first vs manifestless streaming?

maria.chen: index-first still wins for fast random access; it consumes an upfront index credit hit. manifestless streaming gets cheaper steady-state because we only read needed windows. warmup credits let us trade off: operator can set high index-first credit for performance-sensitive models, or low credits to force manifestless streaming + on-demand hydration.

calvin: fallback behavior? suppose credits exhausted mid-request — do we block the request? downgrade?

maria.chen: plan: non-blocking fallback. Router gets a signal `WARMUP_THROTTLE` and can route to: 
- compatible smaller quantized variant (if pinned)
- cached KV prefix snapshot
- queue request behind a short timeout (best-effort)
If none available, we fail fast with a structured error so callers can retry.

rachael: love the structured error idea — please include a machine-readable code so frontend can map to UX states.

maria.chen: agreed: error payload includes `warmup_code`, `estimated_retry_ms`, `available_variant`.

devin.k: implementation boundary question — does warmup-credit live in runtime or loader?

maria.chen: runtime exposes a `WarmupMeter` interface. loader/adapters (safetensors stream parser, index loader, decrypt adapter) call `charge(bytes, tags)` before work. WarmupMeter enforces quota and emits telemetry. This keeps loader logic simple while centralizing policy.

calvin: telemetry we need: credit usage per-model, per-tenant, window hit ratio, hsm spikes, throttled_request_count. add a health SLA metric plumbed to console.

rachael: ops-bot — can we get an alert if warmup throttling > 0.5% of requests in a minute?

ops-bot: created alert `WARMUP_THROTTLE_RATE_HIGH` -> paging on high severity. Link: https://console.internal/alerts/WARMUP_THROTTLE_RATE_HIGH

maria.chen: next steps I see:
- write a small adapter PR that plumbs WarmupMeter through loader interface (I'll draft)
- RFC note: define credit accounting units & weight multipliers (i'll add to RFC doc)
- add router signal `WARMUP_THROTTLE` and fallback mapping (devin to own)
- add console telemetry & alert (rachael to own)

devin.k: i can take router changes. will prototype route fallback to quantized variant first.

calvin: i'll review the adapter PR and help define window-size heuristics for NFS vs blobstore.

rachael: i'll wire alerts + a dashboard with per-model heatmap.

maria.chen: meeting? quick sync tomorrow 11am to align API surface. ping me if you can't. :thumbsup:

devin.k: +1

calvin: +1

rachael: +1
